ruling.recommended_action: Close the case as no action on the fare (fixed RydeX quote, billed distance equals the optimal route), and note in the trip record that one off-route segment (F3) was driven under a rider-agreed named-road reroute whose correspondence to Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5 is not established by any fact (RD-5, G13), while confirming no refundable add-on appears in the fare breakdown.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider's complaint is that a longer way was taken on a fixed-quote RydeX booking [F1][F4][F6]. The trace settles that exactly one off-route segment exists, 21:25–21:32, 4.46 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.34 km (+2.12 km) [F3], so the RD-1 duty to take the shortest and most direct route was engaged and the segment must be screened under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [RD-1].

No RD-4 exemption is available: the trace records no traffic incident on the replaced stretch (✗), and the speed-band facts [F11][F12] are, under RD-4(b), corroborative only and cannot exempt a segment on their own; RD-4(c) therefore sends the segment to RD-2 [RD-4]. The rider's first message, "Sure, no problem." at 21:22, answers the driver's proposal to "go round via Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5" [F7][F8], so this is a specific named-route authorisation rather than a general "whichever way is faster" consent, and it does not rest on the driver's own statement [F10], which under G11 is not consent [RD-5].

The rider's agreement therefore covers driving on Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5 only, and no fact ties the 21:25–21:32 segment to that road: the segment fact gives only times, distances and metres off-route [F3], and the only record naming the road is an LTA speed-band reading for ANG MO KIO AVENUE 5 (band 2, 21:02–21:52) [F12], which is a record of conditions on a road, not of where this vehicle drove. No stop was measured in the segment and no rider message asked for one, so RD-3 does not apply (RD-3(a) requires a rider-named place with the car stopping there) [F7][F8][RD-5]. I therefore leave the segment undetermined (G13, which the trace marks "?" and expressly permits because consent scope changes neither the amount on a fixed fare nor the flag) rather than calling it exempt, since naming it exempt would treat a road-conditions reading as a routing record [RD-5].

The money branch is settled and yields nothing: RydeX is a non-metered fixed-quote service, the billed distance 17.6 km does not exceed the optimal 17.6 km, surge is 1.0×, and the breakdown ($3.90 base + $24.87 distance + $6.71 time + $0.00 waiting + $1.47 platform = $36.95) contains no ERP, toll or unpublished add-on [F4][F5][F6], so RD-2's non-metered branch refunds $0 and FARE-1 has no item to remove [RD-2][FARE-1].

No account flag follows: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, and the driver's profile records route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (2 upheld of 3 disputes, neither a route dispute); profiles cannot decide the case in any event [F17][F16][RD-6]. A zero refund on the only refundable item means the fare and all charged items stand unchanged [RD-2].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's own message at 21:22 ('Sure, no problem.') [F8] answers the driver's proposal naming one road, Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5 [F7], and predates the segment start at 21:25 [F3], so under RD-5 the agreement is a specific named-road authorisation, not a general route choice. No fact ties this segment to Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5: the segment fact [F3] carries no road name, and the speed-band reading for that road [F12] records conditions on the road, not the vehicle's path; no stop on named ground or locating message exists (RD-3(a) inapplicable, no stop measured) [F7][F8]. Nothing places the segment elsewhere, so the scope is undetermined (G13). This changes neither the amount on a fixed RydeX fare [F4][F6] nor the flag [F17], so the case may still be ruled [RD-5][RD-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted in part only: an off-route segment exists [F3][RD-1], but its treatment is not automatically a refundable deviation — RD-5 exempts or leaves undetermined a segment driven under the rider's prior named-route agreement [F7][F8][RD-5]. It also yields no money: RydeX is fixed-quote and RD-2's non-metered branch refunds nothing here [F4][F6][RD-2].

Accepted and used: the consent in F8 is specific to the named road Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5 [F7][F8][RD-5], but this reading does not convert into a refund, because consent scope changes neither the fixed fare nor the flag [F4][F6][F17][RD-2].

Not adopted as a referral: G13 undetermined scope changes neither the amount (fixed fare, billed distance equals optimal) nor the account flag [F3][F4][F6][F17], and the trace allows the case to be ruled, so the segment is recorded undetermined without escalation [RD-5][RD-2].
Accepted: RD-2's non-metered branch and FARE-1 produce no refundable item on this breakdown [F4][F6][RD-2][FARE-1], which itself removes any cash relief the complaint seeks.

Rejected: F12 is an LTA speed-band record of traffic conditions on ANG MO KIO AVENUE 5, not a record of where this vehicle drove; RD-5 requires the record to tie the segment to the named road, and timing alone does not, so the segment is not exempt [F3][F12][RD-5].

Rejected: RD-4(b) makes a speed-band record corroborative only — it cannot exempt a segment standing alone, and the trace marks RD-4(a) failed with no incident on the replaced stretch (F14) [F11][F14][RD-4].

Partly rejected: the $0.00 computation is right, but the premise that the segment is exempt fails — the segment remains undetermined as to consent scope [F3][F7][F8][F12][RD-5]. The outcome is nonetheless no_action because a fixed fare with billed distance equal to the optimal route leaves nothing to refund [F4][F6][RD-2].
